thread:
may: Throwing out a slightly different pattern: "soft-reserve" leases where operator reserves a budget + a compensation_ledger window. runtime redeems and consumes; if operator revokes, compensation covers late consumption for a short window. goal: fewer mid-request failures and simpler operator surface.
jordan: Sounds promising. How is this different from the escrow/lease ideas we've been tossing?
priya: Main diff: explicit compensation ledger + a short "settle" window. operator reserves units and opens a settle window (e.g., 30s). runtime can continue to finish inflight work and post consumes. operator then reconciles against compensation ledger entries before reclaiming.
kevin: So operator remains the single source of truth for allocation, but we allow runtime to finish work without racing on revokes. good. what fields do we need on the lease?
arya: Minimal proto sketch (rough):
```
SoftLease {
  lease_id: string
  tenant_id: string
  reserved_units: int64
  expires_at: int64
  revoke_at?: int64        // optional start of draining
  settle_window_secs: int  // how long compensation is honored after revoke
  safety_flags: string[]   // immutable, e.g. "no-quant", "min-recall:0.92"
  proto_version: string
}

RedeemRequest { lease_id, request_id, wanted_units }
RedeemResponse { accepted_units, provisional_receipt }

Consume { provisional_receipt, used_units }

CompensationEntry { receipt_id, used_units, timestamp }
```
priya: Key semantics: provisional_receipt is signed by operator (or includes operator-signed token) so runtime retries don't double consume. compensation entries are time-bounded and only accepted within settle_window_secs.
jordan: What about operator failures and leader elections? receipts need server-side persistence before ack. if operator crashed after issuing receipt but before persisting, we must tolerate retries. signed receipts + idempotent server semantics required.
kevin: Observability: runtime emits events for redeem/consume/compensation with lease_id, receipt_id, variant_chosen, fallback_reason, trace_id. operator exposes a reconciliation dashboard showing reserved vs consumed vs compensated amounts per-tenant. finance can reconcile easily.
may: Safety_flags must be immutable on issuance. if product says "no-quant" that must be honoured for the lease lifetime. if tenant later wants to relax, they need a new lease. runtime should validate flags against tenant policy before using.
arya: Extra: include "fallback_contract" field on lease (string enum) listing allowed degradations, e.g. "trim-history", "lower-precision", "no-fallback". runtime must follow contract and log when it applies a fallback.
priya: Error surface: STANDARDIZED_CODES = ["LEASE_EXPIRED", "INSUFFICIENT_UNITS", "VIOLATES_SAFETY", "RECEIPT_INVALID", "COMPENSATION_WINDOW_CLOSED"]
kevin: Migration plan idea: 1) operator implements soft-lease API + ledger and provisional_receipt signing; 2) runtime implements redeem/consume and honors safety_flags and fallback_contract; 3) run in advisory mode where runtime logs but doesn't enforce flags; 4) canary tenants flip to enforced mode; 5) enable compensation window and reconcile dashboards.
jordan: A few tough edgecases: long-lived streaming requests that span multiple lease renewals; partial consumes on retries; and cross-data-center clock skew when checking revoke_at/settle windows.
priya: For streaming: require a stream-level receipt that can be checkpointed periodically (e.g., per-1s or per-chunk). operator accepts incremental consumes; reconcile uses receipts timeline. For clock skew, use operator server time as truth and include server timestamps in receipts.
kevin: For partial retries, provisional_receipt must include a nonce + signature; operator ledger stores highest-accepted-nonce per receipt to prevent double-accepts. also attach proto_version so we can change semantics safely.
may: Observability checklist (sampls): per-lease timeseries (reserved, redeemed, consumed, compensated), per-variant cost_by_lease, fallback-audit-log, inflight-drain-traces showing requests crossing revoke boundaries. console drilldown must link to trace_id and receipt_id.
ops-bot: FYI monitoring flagged a headroom shortfall earlier today at 06:07 UTC. 10% of dedicated pools temporarily spilled. incident: https://incidents/7065430001 :warning:
arya: Rollout caveat: compensation_window is a soft safety net, not an excuse to overcommit. operator should expose overcommit thresholds and tenants should opt into short settle windows.
priya: Next concrete actions: I will draft the soft-lease proto (with proto_version and signed provisional_receipts) and a short migration doc mapping capacity_grant -> soft-lease. kevin will prototype redemption endpoints and signed receipt logic. arya will draft fallback_contract enums and product-facing docs. may will draft the reconciliation dashboard queries.
jordan: Let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to review the proto + reconciliation UX.
